post.description:
Execute workflows programmatically to automate business processes, trigger notifications, route interactions, and integrate with external systems.

## Quick Start

### 1. Find Your Customer Subdomain

Your subdomain is found in your Infinity portal URL.

**Example:** If your portal URL is:
```
https://core.avaya1234.ec.avayacloud.com/app/core-config-ui/
```

Your subdomain is: **`avaya1234`**

### 2. Get Your Access Token

Follow the [Access Token API guide](https://developers.avayacloud.com/avaya-infinity/reference/generateaccesstoken) to generate your Bearer token.

### 3. Make Your First Request

Replace `{customer-subdomain}` with your actual subdomain and add your Bearer token to get started.

## Working with Variables

Variables you pass are accessible throughout your workflow execution:

```json
{
  "variables": {
    "customer_name": "John Smith",
    "order_id": "TEST-1984-001",
    "amount": "499.99"
  }
}
```

**Access in Workflow:**
- `{{customer_name}}` → "John Smith"
- `{{order_id}}` → "TEST-1984-001"
- `{{amount}}` → "499.99"

**Common Use Cases:**
- Send data to external systems via webhook modules
- Make routing decisions based on values (amount, status, priority)
- Personalize notifications and messages
- Pass customer context to agents

variables.description: All input variables plus any variables set during execution

outputVariables.description: Variables specifically marked as outputs (only present when completed)

tags.name: Workflow Sessions
tags.description:
Execute and manage workflow sessions for automation and business process integration.

## Rate Limits & Quotas

- **Rate Limit:** 100 requests per minute per customer subdomain
- **Burst Limit:** 20 requests per second
- **Concurrent Sessions:** 1,000 active workflow sessions per subdomain

When rate limited, the API returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

## Best Practices

### 1. Store Session IDs
Always save the returned `sessionId` to check execution status later.

### 2. Handle Asynchronous Execution
Workflows execute asynchronously. Poll for completion using the [Get Workflow Session Status](https://developers.avayacloud.com/avaya-infinity/reference/getworkflowsessionstatus-2) endpoint.

### 3. Validate Input Before Sending
Validate your variables before making the API call to avoid errors.

### 4. Use Meaningful Variable Names
Choose clear, consistent variable names that match your workflow design.

✅ Good: `customer_email`, `order_total`, `shipping_method`  
❌ Avoid: `var1`, `data`, `temp`

### 5. Implement Retry Logic
Handle transient failures with exponential backoff for 429 and 5xx errors.

## Security Best Practices

### ⚠️ Never Expose Tokens Client-Side

Always call the Avaya API from your backend server, never directly from browser JavaScript or mobile apps.

### Filter Sensitive Data

Don't pass sensitive information unless your workflow specifically needs it.

### Use HTTPS Only

Always use `https://` endpoints. Never use unencrypted `http://` connections.
